# Ebook Voice Player

> Ebook Voice Player is a text-to-speech ebook reader for Windows 10 and Windows 11 (x64). It opens TXT, DOCX, PDF, EPUB and HTML books, reads them aloud with 300+ neural voices across 70+ languages, highlights the paragraph being spoken, and can export narration to MP3.

## Key facts

- **App name:** Ebook Voice Player
- **Current version:** {{APP_VERSION}}
- **Platform:** Windows 10 version 1809 (build 17763) or later, Windows 11; x64
- **Distribution:** signed MSIX package in the Microsoft Store
- **Publisher:** {{PUBLISHER}}
- **Supported book formats:** TXT, DOCX, PDF, EPUB, HTML
- **Voices:** 300+ neural voices
- **Languages:** 70+ languages, 140+ regional locales
- **Interface languages:** English, Simplified Chinese
- **Core features:** paragraph highlighting, automatic chapter detection, chapter and paragraph navigation, adjustable speed, text size and line spacing, bookmarks, notes, in-book search, sleep timer, MP3 export
- **Internet:** required for speech synthesis; exported MP3 files play offline
- **Accounts:** none required
- **Data handling:** books are parsed locally; only the text selected for narration is sent to the Microsoft Edge online text-to-speech service. No telemetry or advertising SDKs.
- **System requirements:** Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11, x64 processor, internet connection, audio output device

## About the product

Ebook Voice Player is aimed at readers who want to keep reading while commuting, doing chores, studying or resting their eyes. Unlike tools that convert a book into an audio file before playback begins, the app reads the visible text in place: the current paragraph is highlighted as it is spoken, chapters are detected from the book structure, and playback can start from any paragraph.

Speech is generated on demand by an online neural text-to-speech service, so the app does not ship voice models locally and needs a network connection for new audio. Books themselves are opened and parsed on the device. Users who need offline listening can export chapters or the whole book to MP3.

The application is an independent product and is not affiliated with Microsoft. Microsoft, Windows and Microsoft Store are trademarks of Microsoft Corporation.
